differential: Anemia
A very common cause of fatigue due to reduced oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood, particularly in women.
Hypothyroidism
This condition is prevalent in middle-aged women and causes a generalized slowing of metabolism, leading to fatigue.
Major Depressive Disorder
Fatigue is a core neurovegetative symptom of depression, which is a common cause of chronic constitutional symptoms.
Obstructive Sleep Apnea
Fragmented sleep and intermittent hypoxia result in non-restorative sleep and significant daytime fatigue.
Diabetes Mellitus Type 2
The insidious onset of hyperglycemia and metabolic dysfunction can manifest as persistent fatigue.
eliminated: Acute viral infection
The 6-month duration of symptoms is inconsistent with an acute, self-limiting illness.

differential: Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML)
This myeloproliferative neoplasm classically presents in middle age with fatigue, splenomegaly, and anemia.
Primary Myelofibrosis
This condition causes bone marrow fibrosis, leading to extramedullary hematopoiesis in the spleen (splenomegaly), anemia (pallor/fatigue), and constitutional symptoms like fever.
Hairy Cell Leukemia
This chronic B-cell leukemia is characterized by pancytopenia (causing fatigue and pallor) and significant splenomegaly.
Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma
Certain types of lymphoma can infiltrate the spleen, causing splenomegaly along with B symptoms such as fever and fatigue.
Subacute Bacterial Endocarditis
This chronic infection can present with low-grade fevers, anemia of chronic disease, and splenomegaly due to immune complex deposition.
eliminated: Acute Leukemia
The chronic 6-month duration of fatigue makes an acute process, which typically has a more rapid and severe onset, much less likely.

differential: Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML)
The combination of marked leukocytosis with a left shift, basophilia, splenomegaly, and a low leukocyte alkaline phosphatase score is classic for CML.
Atypical Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (aCML)
This myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasm can mimic CML but is defined by the absence of the BCR-ABL1 fusion gene.
Chronic Neutrophilic Leukemia (CNL)
This is a rare myeloproliferative neoplasm causing high neutrophil counts, but it typically lacks significant basophilia and has a high LAP score.
Primary Myelofibrosis (prefibrotic stage)
This myeloproliferative neoplasm can present with leukocytosis and splenomegaly, but the LAP score is usually normal to high.
Leukemoid Reaction
This is a severe reactive leukocytosis that can mimic CML, but it is strongly argued against by the chronicity of symptoms and the low LAP score.
eliminated: Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML)
The peripheral smear shows a spectrum of maturing granulocytes rather than a predominance of blasts (>20%).
Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)
The leukocytosis is of the myeloid/granulocytic lineage, not the lymphoid lineage.

differential: Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML)

This myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasm can present with splenomegaly and leukocytosis but is characterized by significant monocytosis and lacks the Philadelphia chromosome.
Atypical Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (aCML)
This diagnosis is reserved for CML-like presentations that are, by definition, negative for the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL1 fusion gene.
Primary Myelofibrosis
While this myeloproliferative neoplasm causes splenomegaly and anemia, the blood smear findings are more classic for CML, and it is excluded by the presence of the Philadelphia chromosome.

differential: Anemia
Iron deficiency anemia is a very common cause of fatigue in women, particularly in the perimenopausal age range.
Hypothyroidism
This endocrine disorder commonly presents with fatigue and is most prevalent in middle-aged women.
Depression
Fatigue is a core somatic symptom of major depressive disorder, which is a common condition.
Menopause
Hormonal fluctuations during the menopausal transition are a frequent physiological cause of fatigue and sleep disturbance in women of this age.
Obstructive Sleep Apnea
Unrestorative sleep due to intermittent airway obstruction is a common and often overlooked cause of significant daytime fatigue.
eliminated: Acute Viral Syndrome

differential: Lymphoma
This malignancy is a primary consideration given the presence of a B symptom (fever), chronic fatigue, and pallor suggesting anemia.
Tuberculosis
This chronic infection classically presents with an insidious onset of fatigue, low-grade fevers, and anemia of chronic disease.
Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
This autoimmune disease is common in this demographic and can manifest with constitutional symptoms like fatigue, fever, and hematologic abnormalities.
Occult Malignancy
A solid tumor, such as renal cell carcinoma, can cause a paraneoplastic syndrome with fever, fatigue, and anemia.
Subacute Bacterial Endocarditis
This indolent infection can cause prolonged low-grade fevers, fatigue, and pallor from anemia of chronic inflammation.
